correctness.rationale: For every finite nonempty simple G with chi=omega=k, a k-clique gives L(T_k) as a lower bound for every orientation: its tournament is transitive or has a directed cycle. A k-coloring induces an orientation homomorphism into T_k and the reverse inclusion. T_k accepts exactly signs without k equal consecutive letters by a constructive alternating-run walk. A reachable and Myhill–Nerode-distinguishable complete 2k-state run DFA proves minimality; run-length compositions give the generating function. The k=1 case and C5 boundary are explicit. The standalone enumerator and orientation checker replay all their finite claims; none substitutes for an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Pujol, arXiv:2609.08843v1, introduces the remanent language, proves the directed-cycle lemma and the bipartite special case, and connects monotone membership with chromatic number. The complete all-sign language of every graph with chi=omega, its exact 2k minimal DFA, and its full enumerator are not stated in the relevant inspected material. The present general k>=3 assertion does not follow from monotone-only membership without additional clique/color reasoning. value.rationale: The theorem classifies the entire orientation-intersection language for all graphs with chi=omega, including perfect graphs, showing its surprising collapse to one run-avoidance language for fixed chromatic number. It answers a structural question about the new invariant, computes exact deterministic state complexity and all word counts, and provides a boundary counterexample for unequal invariants. This is a natural infinite-class classification, not a routine table or an arbitrary narrow parameter computation; prior k=2 is explicitly separated.
